messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: streaming-p99-spike in us-west2. p99 streaming latency > 1.5s for multiple routes. Auto-annotations: suspected GPU node degradation (gpunode-45).

kira: I’m on it. Observed p95 ~120ms, p99 jumping to ~1800ms starting 02:14 UTC. Anyone seeing ECC counts?

sasha: digging into telemetry — NVIDIA ECC correctable errors on gpunode-45 spiked from ~2/min to ~75/min around 02:12. Streaming stalls correlate with cache eviction events. Link to grafana: https://grafana.redwood/services/streaming?panel=tail

omar: confirmed. KV cache miss ratio increased on requests routed to gpunode-45. That node services some dedicated pools for large-context models (gpt-xl-8k). If the GPU has intermittent correctables it's dropping frames causing the runtime to recompile or drop KV caches.

kira: impact assessment — looks like 12 customer routes had elevated tail latency, approximate 4% of streaming sessions experienced stalls >1s. Support please prepare a customer list. :exclamation:

support: pulling list now. Affected customers: acme-inc, fastchat.ai, docspark — notifying priority support and sending status page draft.

ryan: infra-bot, what did the automatic mitigation do?

infra-bot: Auto-mitigation executed: 1) traffic split 80/20 redirect off gpunode-45 to fallback pool (cpu-fallback-1 & gpunode-46) 2) incremental qps reduction on gpunode-45 3) scheduled cordon/drain action to prevent new pods on gpunode-45.

kira: good. Can someone run a safe drain and full GPU ECC log capture? Paste nvidia-smi and dmesg snippet.

sasha: attaching quick snippets:

```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
GPU 45:
  ECC Errors
    Volatile:  Correctable: 75  Uncorrectable: 0
    Aggregate: Correctable: 120  Uncorrectable: 1
```

```
[ 02:12:14 ] NVRM: Rm: GPU 0000:41:00.0: GPU has suffered an ECC error, recovering.
[ 02:12:15 ] kernel: PM: GPU memory page fault - inject retry
[ 02:12:18 ] runtime: KV cache invalidation - trace id=abc123
```

omar: that uncorrectable=1 worries me, but it's only one. Pattern of many correctable errors suggests failing DIM or GPU hardware glitch.

kira: priority steps: 1) cordon+drain gpunode-45, 2) confirm no customer sessions remain, 3) either hot-swap GPU or reboot node, 4) continue traffic steering, 5) open vendor ticket. Who does node ops?

ryan: I’ll take node ops. Plan to attempt graceful GPU reset first (nvidia-smi --gpu-reset). If reset doesn’t clear ECC correctables, we’ll hot-swap and RMA. Running `kubectl drain gpunode-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`.

sasha: note — model-serving runtime keeps longer-lived KV caches. Draining will evict pods and force reconnect; streaming sessions will migrate but some sessions may restart from scratch. Recommend: route streaming sessions with stateful reconnection header to fallback pool to minimize user-visible replays.

omar: implemented header routing rule: `x-rr-fallback: true` for in-flight connections; should reduce symmetric stall surface.

kira: Support, update status page: brief summary, current impact, estimated mitigation ETA 20m.

support: status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2175001234 — message sent to active support contacts for affected customers.

infra-bot: Node cordon initiated by ryan at 02:18 UTC. Drain underway. Evicting 14 pods. 10/14 pods rescheduled.

sasha: after partial drain p99 for routes shifted off gpunode-45 dropped from 1800ms -> ~220ms. Residual stalls from a few long-tail sessions that reconnect slowly.

omar: running quick per-pod logs, saw repeated `KVCache::rebuild()` at reconnect time, and a handful of `cuda driver ECC correctable` warnings in container logs.

ryan: attempted `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 45` at 02:25 UTC. Reset returned success but ECC correctable counts remained elevated (correctable went from 75 -> 62 then slowly climbing). Deciding to continue with hardware swap — scheduling hot-swap with on-site tech.

kira: vendor escalation: please open NV ticket and attach ECC logs and dmesg. Ryan reach out to vendor channel.

ryan: NV ticket opened NV-87732 with priority P1. Contacted field ops for GPU replacement. ETA for on-site swap ~3 hours.

omar: interim mitigation ideas: 1) permanently avoid routing hot stateful streaming to gpunode-45 (marked degraded), 2) increase KV cache replication factor for critical routes to prevent single-node cache loss, 3) enable aggressive prefetch for tail segments on fallback pools. These are medium-term config changes — I'll file infra tasks.

sasha: also noticed that small-model routes that didn't use large context weren't affected — confirms issue is tied to long-context KV usage pattern.

support: customers notified of degraded performance and that we have active mitigation and replacement scheduled. No SLA credit pre-decision, monitoring for extended impact.

kira: ok team, handoff to night oncall in 2h. Omar — you'll own follow-through until RMA confirmed?

omar: I’ll own the follow-through and will post updates as vendor progresses. Leaving note for night oncall: if ECC correctables start trending up again after hot-swap, treat as potential batch-level hardware issue and escalate to reliability lead.

ryan: doc'd commands and timestamps in incident binder. Quick runbook additions: - mark node as degraded label `gpu.health=degraded` - automatic traffic split threshold at p99>800ms for 5m - fallback route header `x-rr-fallback`.

kira: thanks. Postmortem owner assigned: sasha. Please include root cause hypothesis, timeline, customer impact, and follow-ups (RMA tracking, KV cache replication, routing rule graduation).

sasha: acknowledged, will have draft within 24h.

pagerbot: Incident resolved? monitoring shows p99 back to baseline ~210ms after drain and traffic split. Will close paging if no regressions in 30m.

kira: moving to monitoring state. If we see new ECC uncorrectable errors or p99 jump >500ms for 10m, escalate immediately. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
